title: Latent Q-Barrier Shielding for Safe In-Context Reinforcement Learning
claim: Our method reaches high reward earlier and lowers constraint violation over adaptation episodes versus baselines, except in one conservative environment.
layout: 2x5 grid of line plots, return over cost, shared legend below
description: A 2-row by 5-column grid of line charts. Columns are benchmarks: SafeDarkRoom, SafetyPoint, SafetyCar, SafetyHalfCheetah and SafetyAnt. The top row plots per-episode Return and the bottom row plots Cost, both against Episode Index k. Five methods appear as colored lines with light shaded standard-error bands: Q-Barrier (Ours) in red, SCARED in blue, Safe AD in green, MAML with penalty in dark red, and Safe Meta in gray. A single legend runs along the bottom. In most return panels the red curve climbs fastest and highest, and in the cost panels it falls quickly to low values. SafetyHalfCheetah is the exception: red sits at lower return and lower cost than blue. The noisy gray and dark red curves hover near the bottom of the return panels. The eye goes first to the red curves.
caption: In-context adaptation dynamics (RQ1). Per-episode return (top) and cost (bottom) over in-context episode index $k$ on test-time evaluation tasks. Curves show means over 100 evaluation tasks, with shaded regions denoting standard error of the mean. Q-Barrier generally improves adaptation by reaching high return earlier and reducing cost after a short context window, while SafetyHalfCheetah shows a conservative Pareto point with lower cost and lower return.
abstract: Safe in-context reinforcement learning (ICRL) adapts online from interaction history without test-time parameter updates while controlling episode cost under a safety budget. Under out-of-distribution (OOD) deployment shifts, pretraining-only safe ICRL can give poor reward-safety tradeoffs because the remaining budget affects behavior only through frozen policy conditioning, not an explicit action-level check against predicted future cost. We propose a latent Q-Barrier shield that learns a context representation, latent dynamics, and an ensemble cost critic before deployment. Without parameter updates, the shield infers context from history and filters or softly reweights candidate actions using the remaining budget and predicted future cost. We prove a conditional one-step barrier-margin bound over realized candidate sets, with explicit Bellman and latent-prediction error terms. Across five safe ICRL benchmarks, the shield improves deployment-time reward-safety tradeoffs over a strong safe-ICRL baseline: after a short context window, it achieves higher return in four of five benchmarks while matching or lowering average episode cost in all five. Code is available at https://github.com/kmj1122/q-barrier.
